title: Lead validation step: its settings panel (#2590, #2588)
intro: The settings panel of the lead validation step, the canvas step that replaces each partner workflow's validate_bidding_and_state script (#934). For whoever builds or edits a partner workflow. Settled by Dan on 2026-10-21 over rounds 1 to 4 of six, drawn inside the real canvas and config panel with RML GigFi's six real checks and Lead Economy's phone check. The step's card on the canvas is settled in lead-validation-node-card.html beside this file.

requirements.text: The lead validation step is on the canvas: a palette entry, a card, and a settings panel holding the lead id field and an ordered list of checks, each edited with the rule builder, a reason from LEAD_REJECTION_REASONS and what happens when the lead has no value.
One shared list of condition operators and their labels feeds the rule builder, the simple Filter condition and every condition summary, and adds the two operators the lead validation checks need.

chrome.from: https://bidspoke.trypennie.dev/workflows/0630d714-5917-4221-9bcc-ca1fb2d9eba2 (Main Flow (v2), switched off) in edit mode with a Filter step's panel open, Dan's signed in Chrome, 2026-10-21

frames.title: The panel with seven checks, check 3 (Name has letters) open

decisions.decision: The checks are a short numbered list under the heading "Checks, in order", with the chosen check edited in one editor below the list, never every check open at once.
decisions.why: Round 1: Dan chose "List on top, editor below" over all open and stacked, and over one line each opened in place.
decisions.check: Under the heading "Checks, in order" there is a list of seven rows numbered 1 to 7 holding the fixture's checks in order, followed by exactly one editor, and the rule builder ("Match:") appears only inside that editor.

decisions.decision: Each list row shows the check's name and a short form of its condition: the field's last segment, the operator in the dropdown's words and the value without its Constants prefix, plus "and N more" when the check has more conditions.
decisions.why: Round 2: Dan chose "Name and condition" over the name with its reason, and over the name alone.
decisions.check: Each row reads its number, the check's name, then its short condition, exactly: Bidding is on / biddingActive is true, State is allowed / state in list states, Name has letters / firstName contains a letter and 1 more, Loan within maximum / loanAmount ≤ maximumLoanAmount, Not military / employmentStatus ≠ military, Self employed / employmentStatus = self_employed, Phone given / primaryPhone is not empty.

decisions.decision: The chosen row is marked in navy: a navy number badge with white text and a navy left edge.
decisions.why: Round 1 drew the chosen check in navy, the app's selection colour (.impeccable.md, #2114); every round after held it.
decisions.check: Row 3's number badge is navy (#1D212F) with white text and its left edge is a 2px navy line; no other row's badge or left edge is navy.

decisions.decision: The editor names which check it holds: "Check N of M".
decisions.why: Held identical in every round from round 1, so the editor says which row it edits.
decisions.check: The editor's first line starts with the text "Check 3 of 7".

decisions.decision: The check's name is edited in a text box on the editor's first line.
decisions.check: The editor's first line holds a text box whose value is the chosen check's name, "Name has letters".

decisions.decision: A check is moved up, moved down and removed from buttons on the editor's first line.
decisions.why: Held identical in every round: the list is ordered, and the order is the order the checks run in.
decisions.check: The editor's first line holds three buttons named Move up, Move down and Remove check, in that order.

decisions.decision: A check's condition is edited with the existing rule builder, as the Branch panel draws it.
decisions.why: Held identical in every round; the issue asks for the existing rule builder.
decisions.check: The editor holds "Match:" with AND and OR buttons, one row per condition of the chosen check (two), each with a field box holding its field, an operator dropdown and a button named Remove condition, and a button reading "Add condition".

decisions.decision: A check is added from an "Add check" button between the list and the editor.
decisions.check: One button reading "Add check" comes after the list's last row and before the editor.

decisions.decision: The row summaries name each operator in the rule builder dropdown's own words, one vocabulary from CONDITION_OPERATOR_SPECS ("=" not "equals"; "in list" and "is true" have words).
decisions.why: Round 3: Dan decided from the measurement, with no round drawn, that cards and summaries use the dropdown's words.
decisions.check: For each condition shown in the editor, the text of its operator dropdown's selected option appears in the chosen row's summary, and no row summary holds a spelled out word (equals, does not equal, greater than, less than, does not contain, does not exist).

decisions.decision: The Filter card on the canvas names its condition's operator in the same dropdown words ("state = x", "state in list CA,NY").
decisions.why: Round 3, as D9: one vocabulary for the dropdown, the Filter card and every condition summary.

decisions.decision: The two new operators are named "contains a letter" (has_letter) and "is not empty" (not_blank), offered last in the operator dropdown, and neither shows a value box.
decisions.why: Round 4: Dan chose "contains a letter, is not empty", which matches the wording of the existing choices (contains, is null), over "has a letter, not blank" and "has letters, has text".
decisions.check: Each operator dropdown in the editor offers the eighteen shared operators in list order, the last two reading "contains a letter" and "is not empty"; both of check 3's conditions show "contains a letter" and have no value box.

decisions.decision: The lead id field is its own field ahead of the checks, saying what the value is for.
decisions.why: Held identical in every round: a rejection sends the lead's id back to the partner.
decisions.check: A field labelled "Lead id field" holds a text box reading trigger.payload.leadUuid with "Sent back as lead_id when a lead is rejected." under it, and comes before the heading "Checks, in order".

decisions.decision: The reason a check rejects with is chosen from a dropdown of LEAD_REJECTION_REASONS, never typed.
decisions.why: Held identical in every round; partners match on the exact reason text (#2588, #935).
decisions.check: A dropdown labelled "Rejects with" shows "invalid name" and offers exactly the nine reasons of LEAD_REJECTION_REASONS in its order.

decisions.decision: What happens when the lead has no value is chosen per check: reject with this reason, let it through, or fail the run.
decisions.why: Held identical in every round; the three outcomes the engine node supports (#2589).
decisions.check: A dropdown labelled "If the lead has no value" shows "Reject with this reason" and offers exactly "Reject with this reason", "Let it through" and "Fail the run".

decisions.decision: Advanced settings are collapsed under one Advanced button at the end of the panel.
decisions.why: Held identical in every round: what sits under it is rarely changed, and the checks are what the panel is for.
decisions.check: A button reading "Advanced", not expanded, comes after the checks, and nothing follows it in the panel body.

idioms: The panel is drawn inside a captured copy of the canvas at 1120 wide; the canvas, the panel's header (type, title, step ID and its three buttons), Display name, Step ID and Test this node are the product as it is today, not decisions.
The dropdowns are drawn with the captured panel's own select styling, as the rule builder draws its operator dropdown today.
